# Le Jour

> Le Jour makes mechanical chronographs and divers with Sellita movements. Prices in CHF include Swiss VAT and import costs. Claim: For those who know.

## History, with sources
- Le Jour ("the day") sold chronographs and divers under its own name from the 1960s and distributed Yema watches in the United States, including Yachtingraf regatta timers signed Le Jour (dealer sources).
- In the 1970s and early 1980s Heuer manufactured chronographs for Le Jour under a private-label arrangement. Source: https://onthedash.chronocentric.com/docs/LeJour.shtml
- A dealer catalogue from June 1980 lists the Le Jour 7203 at USD 300 list and the Heuer Pasadena 750.501 at USD 354 list. OnTheDash calls them the same watch.
- The name returned around 2015 with mechanical watches built around Sellita movements.

## Movements
Sellita SW500 (automatic chronograph, 28'800 vph), SW200 (automatic), SW330 (automatic GMT).

## Lines
- Corsa Master (Piste): Chronograph, 42 mm, Sellita SW500 automatic chronograph, 200 m, from CHF 1'790
- Rally Monte-Carlo (Piste): Chronograph, 40 mm, Sellita SW500 automatic chronograph, 100 m, from CHF 1'790
- Roadster (Piste): Chronograph, 42 mm, Sellita SW500 automatic chronograph, 200 m, from CHF 1'490
- Delmare (Mer): Diver, 41 mm, Sellita SW200 automatic, 200 m, from CHF 1'090
- Seacolt (Mer): Diver, 42 mm, Sellita SW200 automatic, 200 m, from CHF 990
- Hammerhead (Mer): GMT, 42 mm, Sellita SW330 automatic GMT, 200 m, from CHF 1'290
- Brooklyn (Ville): Automatic, 40 mm, Sellita SW200 automatic, 100 m, from CHF 990
- Fardón (Ville): Automatic, 38 mm, Sellita SW200 automatic, 50 m, from CHF 1'490
- Heritage (Ville): Automatic, 42 mm, Sellita SW200 automatic, 100 m, from CHF 890

## Service
Five-year warranty, transferable. 30 days to return, free to a Swiss address. Delivered duty paid to Switzerland by Swiss Post in 2 to 4 working days. Payment: TWINT, invoice, cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal.
